model_organism.citation: Kcnq3 knockout mouse study - KCNQ3 is the principal target of retigabine in CA1 and subicular excitatory neurons (PMID: 33729829)
phenotypes: Deletion of Kcnq3 severely limited the ability of retigabine to reduce neuronal excitability in CA1 and subiculum excitatory neurons
In the absence of KCNQ3, retigabine enhanced CA1 pyramidal neuron activity, producing more action potentials and reduced spike frequency adaptation

model_organism.citation: Place fields of single spikes in hippocampus involve Kcnq3 channel-dependent entrainment of complex spike bursts (PMID: 34376649)
phenotypes: Pyramidal cell bursts less coordinated by theta rhythm during spatial navigation, but not during alert immobility
Intact post-burst pause of single spike firing, causing temporal discoordination of network oscillations and intrinsic excitability
Smaller place fields of single spikes in one- and two-dimensional environments
Altered burst and single-spike representations that may contribute to cognitive deficits

model_organism.citation: Contribution of KCNQ2 and KCNQ3 to the medium and slow afterhyperpolarization currents (PMID: 19060215)
phenotypes: ImAHP not impaired in CA1 pyramidal neurons of KCNQ3-deficient (or KCNQ2-deficient) mice
ImAHP reduced about 50% in dentate granule cells of KCNQ-deficient mice
Calcium-activated slow AHP current (IsAHP) also reduced in dentate granule cells

model_organism.citation: Loss of KCNQ2 or KCNQ3 Leads to Multifocal Time-Varying Activity in the Neonatal Forebrain Ex Vivo (PMID: 33863780)
phenotypes: Constitutive Kcnq3 deletion led to sprawling hyperactivity across the neocortex in neonatal brain slices
Neocortical activity in Kcnq3 knockouts remained primarily driven by fast synaptic transmission
Hypersynchronous activity in the hippocampal formation persisted with synaptic transmission blockers
Region-specific network hyperactivity across the forebrain

biological.citation: Expression and function of KCNQ channels in larval zebrafish (PMID: 21692188)
biological.summary: qPCR and whole-mount in situ hybridization showed KCNQ2, 3 and 5 mRNA in zebrafish brain between 2 and 7 dpf. Morpholino knockdown of KCNQ3 confirmed a role for KCNQ channels in generating electrical burst discharges. Kv7 inhibitors (linopirdine, XE991) induced burst discharges and convulsive behavior, and retigabine blocked them.

biological.citation: Immunohistochemical analysis of KCNQ3 potassium channels in mouse brain (PMID: 16513263)
biological.summary: An N-terminal KCNQ3 antibody showed widespread immunoreactivity in adult mouse brain, mainly neuropil but also somata, in hippocampus, cortex, thalamus and cerebellum. Staining increased gradually during development. In hippocampal pyramidal cells it shifted from somatic to neuropil, which may relate to the age-dependent BFNC phenotype.

biological.citation: Triclosan is a KCNQ3 potassium channel activator (PMID: 35459955)
biological.summary: Triclosan activates KCNQ3 but not KCNQ2. It shifts the voltage dependence of activation, increases conductance and slows channel closing, independently of PIP2. Docking and mutagenesis place the binding site in the voltage-sensor domain.

biological.citation: Lipophilic compounds restore function to neurodevelopmental-associated KCNQ3 mutations (PMID: 39300259)
biological.summary: Voltage clamp fluorometry, MD simulations and electrophysiology showed that NDD-associated KCNQ3 variants alter gating either by affecting S4 movement or by changing S4-to-pore coupling. PUFAs target the activated voltage-sensing domain. They partially restored function in R227Q channels and fully restored it in R236C channels.

biological.citation: Electrophysiological Abnormalities and Pharmacological Corrections of Pathogenic Missense Variants in KCNQ3 (PMID: 40095209)
biological.summary: Patch-clamp of 24 KCNQ3 missense variants showed that pore-domain variants cause near-complete loss of function and are associated with self-limited familial neonatal epilepsy. Variants with leftward-shifted V1/2 (gain of function), including the novel G553R, are associated with NDD. Loss-of-function variants were rescued by pynegabine (HN37), and the gain-of-function variant was corrected by amitriptyline.

biological.citation: Altered KCNQ3 potassium channel function caused by the W309R pore-helix mutation found in human epilepsy (PMID: 18425618)
biological.summary: Homomeric KCNQ3 W309R channels lacked current. Heteromeric KCNQ2/KCNQ3 W309R channels showed dominant-negative current suppression and altered gating. Homology modeling suggests the mutation disrupts the pore helix–selectivity filter interaction.

biological.citation: A novel KCNQ3 mutation in familial epilepsy with focal seizures and intellectual disability (PMID: 25524373)
biological.summary: The KCNQ3 R330L variant segregated with early-onset epilepsy and intellectual disability in a family. Electrophysiology in mammalian cells showed impaired channel function, more severe than that of R330C, which causes typical BFNS. The degree of functional impairment may therefore track clinical severity.

biological.citation: Cilantro leaf harbors a potent potassium channel-activating anticonvulsant (PMID: 31311306)
biological.summary: (E)-2-dodecenal from cilantro activates the neuronal KCNQ2/KCNQ3 channel with an EC50 of about 60 nM. It binds between the S5 segment and the S4-5 linker and delays PTZ-induced seizures.

biological.citation: ASHG 2018 - Large-scale targeted sequencing identifies risk genes for autism and developmental delay
biological.summary: Targeted sequencing of 18,836 NDD cases (ASD and DD) found KCNQ3 among genes with increased burden of gene-disruptive and severe missense mutations compared with ExAC controls.

biological.citation: Differential Dorsolateral Prefrontal Cortex Proteomic Profiles of Suicide Victims with Mood Disorders (PMID: 32120974)
biological.summary: KCNQ3 was the top differentially expressed protein in the DLPFC, reduced in male suicide cases with mood disorders versus non-suicide mood disorder controls. Western blot showed a trend to downregulation.
biological.sample_size: 5 suicide vs 5 non-suicide mood disorder cases
biological.significance: Log2FC=-0.481, p=2.10e-09, FDR=5.93e-06; Western blot p=0.045 (Bonferroni 0.090)
